The core insight of Sync-Rank lies in transforming discrete rank differences into continuous angular representations on the unit circle, enabling spectral analysis via eigenvector decomposition. This approach mitigates noise by leveraging the SO(2) symmetry of angular data, where small perturbations do not drastically alter global structure. The method operates under two regimes: one where the top eigenvector reliably estimates true rankings (when 1-η > 1/√n), and another where it fails due to excessive noise. For GSE, this translates into a robust mechanism for aggregating heterogeneous rating sources—engine model probabilities, Elo differences, and market-implied tiers—into a unified ranking. The SDP relaxation offers improved accuracy but at higher computational cost; thus, the eigenvector variant is preferred for real-time applications. In constrained settings, such as anchoring playoff teams, the SDP formulation allows for incorporating prior knowledge without compromising overall coherence. The failure mode arises when noise dominates signal, causing misalignment between estimated and actual rankings, which manifests as high upset counts and low correlation scores.
